title: Projection formula: the pro-étale realization
statement:
Fix the standing finite-field and coefficient setting of [sk-def-sf-setting], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. At a coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, with finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. At finite coefficients use their pro-etale realizations with bounded constructible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]; at the integral stage use the derived-complete completed-coefficient category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with the finite-level etale-origin witnesses, and at the two field stages use [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The concrete projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], computed with a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$, is an isomorphism:
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{c}:Rf_!^{c}K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow Rf_!^{c}(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L).
$$
This holds for every such compactification, hence for the chosen realization denoted $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$. At finite coefficients the assertion is in $D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$; at integral coefficients pullback and tensor are completed, and the assertion is in the derived-complete integral category; at field coefficients it is in the rationalized or common-stage category just specified. No discrete constant-$\mathcal O_E$ etale realization is substituted for the completed integral category.

proof.text: The standing setting is [sk-def-sf-setting]. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0,k$, and its spectrum has one point. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian. By [sk-thm-nagata-sketch-noetherian], compactifications of $f$ exist. Fix any compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $p$ proper. Since proper includes finite type, the same finite-type/Noetherian lemma gives that $\overline X$ is Noetherian. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to the triangle $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$: $f$ is finite type, $p$ is separated, and $j$ is open, so $j$ is quasi-compact. Write $M=j_!K$. By the displayed definition in [def-exchange-projection], the projection map for this compactification is the ordered composite $Rp_*(\gamma_{K,L})\circ\pi_{p;M,L}$, with $\pi$ the counit-defined proper projection map and $\gamma$ the open-extension tensor comparison followed by $Lj^*Lp^*\simeq Lf^*$. We prove invertibility of this specified composite at each coefficient stage; the integral stage below is the cited integral theorem for this same composite, so invertibility of its two factors separately is not needed.

source.place: chosen-compactification expansion of the projection transformation; Stacks Tag 01T6 for Noetherianity

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ choose the stipulated bounded constructible etale representatives $K_0,L_0$ and the witness isomorphisms. If witnesses are instead given intrinsically, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies representatives in the bounded constructible etale category. Since $L_0$ is bounded below, [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) reflects the given finite Tor interval of $L$ to $L_0$. Thus the representatives satisfy precisely the hypotheses of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]: the same finite-field datum, the finite ring $A_{E,n}$, separated finite-type $f$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, bounded constructible $K_0,L_0$, and finite Tor amplitude of the second representative $L_0$. The current cited statement requires no Tor bound on $K_0$; no reflection for the first representative is needed. Its pro-etale realization clause asserts the same canonical compact-support projection formula for their witnessed pro-etale realizations. Its final sentence identifies that transformation with the finite constant-coefficient composite of [def-exchange-projection], namely the composite fixed in step 1 for the chosen compactification. Thus this is a statement about the actual map, not just an isomorphism between its endpoints. Apply the witnessed clause and conjugate by the witness isomorphisms; naturality identifies the conjugated map with the component for K,L, and its inverse is the conjugate of the witnessed inverse. This proves the finite-stage assertion. No assertion about completed integral coefficients follows from this finite-coefficient comparison.

source.place: finite-stage transport; finite-etale projection formula and witnessed pro-etale clause

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ work in the completed-coefficient category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: $K,L$ are derived-complete bounded constructible integral complexes, and membership in $D^b_{ctf}$ means, by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], that their derived reductions $K_n,L_n$ have Tor amplitude in intervals independent of $n$. (For an arbitrary integral bounded constructible object this holds automatically by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], which gives $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(-,\mathcal O_E)$; step 4 uses this.) These are exactly the hypotheses of [thm-sf-pf-adic]: the same finite-field datum, $\ell\ne p$, finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a separated finite-type morphism $f$ of finite-type $k$-schemes (no separatedness of $X,Y$ over $k$), the completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, completed pullback and tensor, and the compact-support direct image and projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection] formed at a chosen compactification. Take as that choice the compactification $c=(j,p)$ fixed in step 1; the superscript $c$ in [def-exchange-projection] records an arbitrary choice. Then [thm-sf-pf-adic] states that $\operatorname{PF}^c_{f,K,L}:Rf^c_!K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}L\to Rf^c_!(K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}Lf^*L)$ is an isomorphism, and that its derived reduction at every $n\geq1$ is $\operatorname{PF}^c_{f,K_n,L_n}$ under the canonical operation comparisons. Since $c$ was arbitrary, this is the integral assertion for every compactification, in the derived-complete integral category with completed pullback and tensor; no discrete constant-$\mathcal O_E$ realization is used. This is the integral stage of the unit's non-finite route (the unit sk-thm-sf-pf-field cites sk-thm-sf-pf-adic, whose statement is [thm-sf-pf-adic]).

For $\Lambda=E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] is the raw scalar localization with the same objects as the integral category, so choose integral bounded constructible representatives $K_0,L_0$ of $K,L$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] they lie in $D^b_{ctf}(-,\mathcal O_E)$, with uniform finite-level Tor intervals; no additional lattice hypothesis is imposed. Apply [thm-sf-pf-field] to these integral representatives: its coefficient categories are exactly the raw rationalization and common-stage categories of this item, and its geometric hypotheses require separatedness of $f$, not of the structure maps of $X$ and $Y$. Its rational clause gives invertibility of the rational projection transformation. For the compactification $c$ fixed in step 1 argue directly: step 3 applied to $(K_0,L_0)$ gives the integral isomorphism $p_0=\operatorname{PF}^c_{f,K_0,L_0}$ with an inverse $b_0$; apply the localization functor $Q_Y$ to both. By functoriality $Q_Y(b_0)Q_Y(p_0)=1$ and $Q_Y(p_0)Q_Y(b_0)=1$. Rational compact support is the localized integral compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and the rationalization compatibility of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] preserves the operation comparisons, tensor associators, units and counits. Substituting these in the two explicit factors of [def-exchange-projection] identifies $Q_Y(p_0)$ with the rational component $\operatorname{PF}^c_{f,K,L}$, not merely its endpoints. Thus that component is invertible. The condensed separated-scheme theorem det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing is not applied to this raw category: its coefficient and scheme hypotheses do not permit that substitution.

source.place: Field continuation named in the unit paragraph: rationalization of the completed integral formula, written explicitly in the raw scalar-localized coefficient category.

proof.text: For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents $K,L$ over finite coefficient fields, and their compositum gives a common finite field $F$. Apply step 4 at $F$. The common-stage clause of [thm-sf-pf-field] states that this finite-stage projection transformation gives the canonical algebraically closed projection map independently of its presentation; its hypotheses hold because both common-stage inputs are represented by integral bounded constructible objects under the same-object rationalization definition. The common-stage scalar-extension compatibility in [lem-fix-operation-reduction], with the morphism convention of [def-exchange-projection], identifies the resulting projection map with the representative of $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{c}$ in the common-stage category. Represent the inverse by the inverse map at $F$. Both composite identities already hold at $F$, so their classes are identities by the displayed Hom-colimit and composition rule in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus the class is invertible, with no construction of an infinite discrete coefficient sheaf and no unproved reflection of isomorphisms by scalar extension. The compactification in step 1 was arbitrary, so all four stages hold for every compactification and hence for the fixed one underlying the notation in the item.

source.place: algebraically closed continuation at a common finite coefficient stage
